articles.title: Jeremiah Smith Labeled 'Perfect Blend' of Terrell Owens, Julio Jones, Andre Johnson by NFL Exec
articles.summary: Multiples NFL scouts have compared wide receiver Jeremiah Smith to Andre Johnson and Julio Jones during his junior season at Ohio State, ESPN's Jordan Reid reported Friday.
articles.body:
Multiples NFL scouts have compared wide receiver Jeremiah Smith to Andre Johnson and Julio Jones during his junior season at Ohio State, ESPN's Jordan Reid reported Friday.

According to Reid, one NFC assistant general manager described Smith as "dominant from the moment he touched the field like Larry [Fitzgerald]."

"He's like a perfect football blend of Julio Jones, Andre Johnson and Terrell Owens," the assistant GM said, per Reid.

Reid described references to Jones and Johnson as "the two most popular comparisons to Smith from scouts I've talked to over the past few months."

That might be a sign Smith has achieved his goal of becoming more of a YAC threat, which he said this summer would be a focus during his junior season.

Smith, listed as the top overall prospect on Bleacher Report's 2027 NFL draft big board , has yet to slow down since a historic freshman season during which he helped the Buckeyes win a national title.

After contributing 95 receiving yards per game as a sophomore, Smith is up to 140 receiving yards per game through seven contests of his junior season.

He is heading into this weekend ranked second among all college wide receivers with 984 receiving yards and 12 touchdown passes.

Smith may be playing without Julian Sayin for the near future given that the quarterback has been labeled out indefinitely after suffering a right arm injury two weeks ago.

Ohio State coach Ryan Day has yet to confim whether Luke Fahey or Tavien St. Clair will be starting in Sayin's place at USC this Saturday. Whether Smith is able to continue producing despite the quarterback turnover could further influence scouts' opinions of him as a potential top pick in the 2027 NFL draft.

articles.title: Rangers v Aberdeen: Can Robinson work Hampden magic in semi-final?
articles.summary: Under-pressure Aberdeen manager Stephen Robinson has an excellent record in Hampden semi-finals. But is Saturday's meeting with Rangers a bridge too far?
articles.body:
Ten months ago Stephen Robinson could have walked into a Paisley pub and expected a standing ovation and to drink for free all night.

In December the Northern Irishman masterminded St Mirren's second ever League Cup triumph , when his relentless and perfectly drilled side dismantled Celtic.

The pictures in the Hampden dressing room afterwards showed Robinson jumping and singing with his team after reaching the crowning moment of his tenure at the club.

It was an altogether different Robinson which appeared in front of the cameras on Wednesday night, after his Aberdeen side lost at home to Falkirk , the fourth time in six home league games they have failed to score.

Questioned about his future, his answers were short and deflated but he acknowledged patience with his team is wearing thin.

There would be no free drink forthcoming in the Pittodrie Bar for the Aberdeen boss after three wins in 11 to start the Premiership season.

Nonetheless, the arrival of Saturday's Premier Sports Cup semi-final against Rangers represents an opportunity to change the gloomy narrative.

Premier Sports Cup semi-final: Rangers v Aberdeen

Live commentary on BBC Radio Scotland, and follow the action on BBC Sport app and website.

Are Aberdeen capable of Robinson-style win?

Robinson was more bullish in his media conference on Friday , pointing to his Hampden record and ability to motivate players for big occassions, and he has a point.

As a manager, he is unbeaten in semi-finals at Scotland's national stadium.

He must now channel that to try to upset Rangers and overcome Derek McInnes, a familiar rival who he has bested in cup competitions before.

Last season Robinson's St Mirren knocked out McInnes' title-chasing Hearts, on penalties, in this very competition on their way to lifting the trophy.

When in charge of Motherwell in 2017-18, his team reached both national cup finals, hammering McInnes' Aberdeen 3-0 in the quarter-finals of the League Cup and the semi-finals of the Scottish Cup.

Pedro Caixinha's Rangers were beaten 2-0 in the semi-final of the former that same season.

In the League Cup semi-finals 12 months ago he constructed a gameplan to completely overrun Motherwell. One of the standout sides of last term under the innovative Jens Berthel Askou, the Steelmen were demolished 4-1 at Hampden.

Then came the crowning achievment, the 3-1 final win over Celtic which was as comprehensive a final defeat the serial trophy winners have had at Hampden in over a decade.

Robinson's ability to prevail in a one-off test should not be underestimated, and McInnes said as much this week. Beware of Robinson the underdog.

"I have done it before - every semi or final I have been in the teams that I was with, Motherwell and St Mirren, were not expected to win," Robinson said.

"So I know how to motivate teams, the staff know how to get teams to believe."

Robinson urges Aberdeen to seize Hampden chance

McInnes defends Fernandez before League Cup semi

Nonetheless the question is whether this Aberdeen team as currently assembled have it in them to produce the type of performance Robinson's teams of the past have put in to claim these notable scalps.

Toughness, organisation, relentless running, and incisive direct attacking at the right times are not qualities this team have shown regularly.

Rather than a clear identity, Robinson has appeared to struggle to know his best team, formation, and approach. Half-time changes and tweaks have been common.

Defensively and at set-pieces the numbers say they have improved on last season, but their creativity and goalscoring has not. And when they have opened up, like against Dundee United a week ago, their defence has suffered.

The absence of defender Mats Knoester in particular is a grievous blow to Aberdeen's hopes of staying resilient in the face of a Rangers team which is unbeaten in 10 games and scoring more goals than when the sides last met at Pittodrie at the end of August.

The frustrated Red Army will be vastly outnumbered at Hampden as they travel south in faint hope of Robinson working his magic in Mount Florida.

If he were to manage it in these cicrumstances, it would not just be another magnificent achievment but a potential turning point in his Aberdeen career.

McInnes under pressure to deliver trophy

While Robinson's position has been relentlessly scrutinised, this semi-final is no less important for Rangers boss McInnes.

One league title, one Scottish Cup, and one League Cup in 14 years is an embarrassing trophy return for Rangers given the money the club have spent.

McInnes is the latest manager charged with changing that after two trophyless campaigns at Ibrox, last season being the first under American ownership who have invested heavily.

Despite consistently showing his managerial abilities, in particular when almost winning a sensational title with Hearts last term, McInnes only has one major trophy to show for it.

That was the League Cup he won in 2014 when in charge of Aberdeen, who he led to Hampden regularly, only to come up against Treble-winning Celtic sides at every turn.

Now, though, Rangers' rivals have already been dispatched 3-0 in the quarter-finals , a rousing win at Ibrox which helped change the direction of their season.

Rangers have created the chance for themselves to claim silverware at the first attempt this season - and they simply must take advantage.

"To get the first trophy would be so important, reinforcing confidence, reinforcing belief," the Rangers boss admitted.

"Traditionally, semi-finals can be fraught with a lot of nerves and tension and sometimes they're not the best games, because of what's at stake."

McInnes is leading an expensively assembled but relatively inexperienced team, and at times they were spooked at a raucous Tynecastle on Wednesday as they were fortunate to claim a late draw.

But in the two Old Firm wins this season, they looked physically dominant and completely assured. McInnes needs his team to deal with the occasion again.

A slip now against a struggling Aberdeen will set him and this Rangers team back, and hard-earned trust with fans will disappear.

Win, though, and a December final date against Hearts or Hibernian presents a magnificent opportunity for McInnes to make an early mark at Ibrox.

articles.title: Newport 4-1 Chesterfield
articles.summary: Newport cruised to a 4-1 victory over Chesterfield at Rodney Parade thanks to a first-half goal blitz.
articles.body:
Right-back Cameron Norman got the ball rolling with a hammer of a free-kick that fizzed into the bottom corner to put County ahead in the 14th minute.

It was 2-0 four minutes later when left-back Tom Davies controlled a loose ball in the box and managed to hook a shot past Zach Hemming in the Chesterfield goal.

Harrison Biggins added a third after half an hour when he tried his luck from distance and caught out Hemming, despite his shot lacking power.

And Yahya Bamba capped a remarkable first half for the hosts as he took advantage of some static defending to curl a delightful finish beyond Hemming in the second minute of stoppage time.

Chesterfield boss Paul Cook was sent off during the interval and his side appeared to be denied two penalties for apparent handballs.

Liam Mandeville's fine finish just before the hour was scant consolation for the visitors.

articles.title: Giroud coloca al Lille de Davide Ancelotti a dos puntos del PSG
articles.standfirst: El galo anotó en la recta final el único tanto del partido
articles.summary: El galo anotó en la recta final el único tanto del partido
articles.body: A sus 40 años, Olivier Giroud sigue estando vigente. El delantero galo entró en el minuto 73 y anotó el único tanto del partido (1-0) ante el Lens. El Lille de Davide Ancelotti, mientras, suma tres puntos clave para romper su racha de empates y se coloca a dos puntos del PSG, que es líder de la liga francesa en solitario. El partido se resolvió en el 86'. Un disparo lejano de Bentaleb, un mal despeje de Risser (que estaba siendo el mejor del Lens) y un Giroud listísimo, el que más de la clase, para anticiparse a la defensa y cazar una volea que hizo el 1-0 definitivo. Davide Ancelotti, que observaba desde la banda amonestado y en claro clima de tensión, estalló de alegría. Un triunfo clave para superar al Rennes, colocarse segundo a dos puntos del PSG y viajar a Bodo con un subidón anímico para el compromiso de Champions League. El Lille, mientras, suma únicamente una derrota esta temporada en Ligue 1: ante el Niza.

articles.title: Sheffield United 1-0 Wrexham: Ben Brereton Diaz's goal enough to earn Blades first league win against Wrexham in 44 years
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Sheffield United and Wrexham at Bramall Lane; Ben Brereton Diaz scored the only goal of the game; Wrexham had only one shot on target as the Blades moved up to 10th
articles.body:
It is a fixture that is turning in to one of the great EFL contests, but after their two Championship matches last term produced 11 goals, this one registered just five shots on target.

The majority were for the Blades, with Brentford loanee Romelle Donovan central to much of the good attacking play, although it was Ben Brereton Diaz who decided it.

He turned home a saved effort from Jordan Ayew for his third goal in three appearances against Wrexham, having scored in both games against them for Derby last season.

Sheffield United should have had a penalty soon after after when Dominic Hyam fouled Harrison Burrows inside the area. However, the referee waved away the claims.

Sam Smith was introduced for Wrexham at the break and the Welsh side looked brighter after, but still only mustered one shot on target - coming in the 96th minute - as they extended their winless away run to five games.

Phil Parkinson cut a disappointed figure after the game, telling Sky Sports : "We haven't got that kind of Wrexham feeling in our performances where everybody's against us, everybody wants to beat us, we've got to fight harder and we've done it on several occasions, but not enough. You've got to do it every week."

The win sees the Blades move to within a point of the play-off places in 10th ahead of the remaining weekend games.

Wrexham remain in 17th with difficult fixtures against Middlesbrough and Wolves over the next eight days, although both are at home.

Parkinson: We have to look at ourselves closely and be honest

Wrexham boss Phil Parkinson to Sky Sports: "First half, we were second best all over the pitch. We've got to take a long look at ourselves for that because they were first to the ball, they were sharper, they closed down with more intent and as I always say to the lads, you know, I look at myself, but the performance in the first half was well below the standard.

"Coming to Bramall Lane, you've got to be ready for the intensity, being all over the pitch, winning your duels, your individual battles first and foremost to give you a foothold in the game.

"The second half was a lot better, but we're disappointed with that first 45 minutes because that wasn't how a Wrexham team plays or has played.

"We've got to turn up every week because it's a relentless division. Actually, you've got to turn up every week in any division and you've got to be ready.

"It's very easy in football to say 'oh the system, we should have done this', but let's look at ourselves first as individuals and could we have done better or were they just better than us? Were they just a better team than us or did they play in that first period with more hunger and desire? And we've got to look closely and be honest."

On the goal and if Anthony Patterson could have done better: "I honestly haven't looked at that back, but you can't criticise Patto for his performance tonight.

"He came and caught crosses, his handling was really good and sometimes a goalkeeper needs help in those situations, whether he could have partnered it around the post. I thought he put in a very solid performance."

Wilder: Players picked up from second half vs Derby

Sheffield United boss Chris Wilder to Sky Sports: "The intent and approach was really good… I asked them to start the game as we finished it second half against Derby and they did. High up the pitch, got the press right.

"We understood that it was going to be a difficult second half. I've just said to the players, we're just a little bit loose on that first pass out.

"There was always going to be a reaction because they've won games of football for a long time and they're no mugs and they've got a real spirit about them. They had five or 10 minutes in the second half, we saw that out.

"We kept the ball and looked after the ball a little bit better then. They had nothing to lose, we had everything to lose. Sometimes you can have to defend and we did make a change late on. Michael [Cooper] has not had a lot to do in terms of saves."

On Ben Brereton Diaz: "I've known Ben for a long time. I know what his qualities are, I know what his character is like.

"I know where he started as a centre-forward in the early part of his career when he got his move to Blackburn. I've tracked his career right the way through. There's a lot of clubs in the division that were after him and delighted that he chose us.

"Not everybody hits the ground running. Not any player, whatever division they are, sometimes get themselves going but that'll do them no harm.

"I thought the performance of the two at the top of the pitch was really good, especially first half. They linked well, stretched well and the better team won the game of football."

Sheffield United goalscorer Ben Brereton Diaz to Sky Sports: "It's nice to get off the mark. The lads were brilliant today from start to finish. We put a good shift in and we need to build on that. We go into a good week and then the international break is coming.

"I knew that I scored a couple against them last year so I hoped I could get one tonight and get off the mark. It's brilliant."

On backing from Chris Wilder: "The gaffer is unbelievable. This is my third time with him at Sheffield United. I love it here. The lads are unreal. It's a great place to be, we just need to build and everyone stay together."

articles.title: Al Villarreal se le atraganta La Cerámica
articles.standfirst: Los amarillos firman uno de sus peores arranques para sumar sólo 4 puntos en su feudo
articles.summary: Los amarillos firman uno de sus peores arranques para sumar sólo 4 puntos en su feudo
articles.body: Los pitos que se escucharon por parte del público en La Cerámica al final del partido fueron el mejor reflejo de la temporada que los amarillos están firmando como locales. Y es que la derrota ante el Espanyol agrava el peor arranque reciente del Villarreal en casa: apenas cuatro puntos en sus cinco primeros partidos como local El resultado y la mala imagen vista ante el Espanyol confirma que el Villarreal ha perdido buena parte de la fortaleza que tradicionalmente encontraba en La Cerámica. Un nuevo golpe en “casa” para los de Íñigo Pérez, que continúan sin encontrar la regularidad necesaria ante su afición y firman uno de los arranques ligueros más discretos de su trayectoria reciente como locales. El tropiezo frente al conjunto perico deja al Submarino con apenas cuatro puntos después de sus cinco primeros encuentros en casa. Un balance de una victoria, un empate y tres derrotas que refleja las dificultades que está encontrando el equipo para convertir su estadio en un escenario fiable. La cifra adquiere mayor dimensión al echar la vista atrás. El Villarreal había atravesado otros comienzos complicados en casa, aunque tan sólo los registros de las campañas 2018/19 y 2023/24 fueron todavía inferiores, con tres puntos en el mismo tramo de competición. La situación actual supone, en cualquier caso, una señal de alarma. La Cerámica, que durante años fue uno de los principales argumentos competitivos del conjunto amarillo, se ha convertido en un escenario donde los puntos se escapan con demasiada facilidad. Íñigo Pérez tiene ahora el reto de recuperar la versión más fiable de su equipo ante su afición. Porque para aspirar a los objetivos marcados esta temporada, el Villarreal necesita volver a hacer de su estadio un fortín

articles.title: Iván Fresneda asiste en el triunfo del Sporting CP
articles.standfirst: Se colocan a seis puntos del Oporto
articles.summary: Se colocan a seis puntos del Oporto
articles.body: No saltó la sorpresa en el derbi lisboeta entre Casa Pia y Sporting CP. Los del Alvalade, jugando a domicilio, se impusieron 0-2 para colocarse a seis puntos del Oporto, que sigue líder y tiene un partido pendiente. Iván Fresneda asistió en el primer gol del Sporting. Un triunfo para recuperar sensaciones en liga. Después de perder en casa ante el Academico Viseu, el Sporting CP necesitaba ganar al Casa Pia a domicilio para no olvidarse de la liga portuguesa en noviembre. Y lo hizo... sufriendo. Un inicial gol de Pedro Lima al cuarto de hora de partido encarriló el duelo. Iván Fresneda, internacional español, asistió con un disparo que acabó en centro y el mediapunta brasileño metió la punta de la bota para anotar el único gol del partido. Sentenció Catamo con el 0-2, ya en el descuento y con el portero local sumándose al ataque. Una victoria que deja al equipo de Altimira y Fresneda, ambos titulares, a seis puntos del Oporto, líder... pero con un partido más que los 'Dragones'.

articles.title: El Ibiza luce su gran pegada en Can Misses
articles.standfirst: El golazo de Josep Calavera dejó sin respuesta al Europa
articles.summary: El golazo de Josep Calavera dejó sin respuesta al Europa
articles.body: La Unión Deportiva Ibiza recuperó la sonrisa en la décima jornada del Grupo 2 de Primera Federación con una victoria rotunda por 3-0 ante el CE Europa, un resultado que refleja con fidelidad el dominio celeste a lo largo de los noventa minutos y que empuja al conjunto balear hacia la zona noble de la clasificación. FICHA TÉCNICA UD Ibiza: Andrés Prieto; Astals, Blasco, Erik, Víctor Prieto; Théo Valls, Calavera, Pedro Ortiz; Mazeya, Javi Eslava y Yoldi. Cambios: Genaro por Pedro Ortiz (56), Manu Justo por Javi Eslava (65'), Varela por Yoldi (65'), Lazo por Mazeya (75') y Fadel por Calavera (75'). Europa: Nil Ruiz; Coto, Cano, Sgró, Campeny, Padillo; Morales, Mascaró, Gori; Khalid y Zayzoun. Cambios: Tolosa por Morales (65'), Expósito por Zayzoun (65'), Marc Anglès por Coto (73'), Pallarés por Sgró (83') y Cardelús por Padillo (83'). Árbitro: José David Martínez. Amonestó con tarjeta amarilla a Fadel, por parte local, y a Padillo, por parte visitante. Goles: 1-0, Calavera (8'). 2-0, Mazeya (51'). 3-0, Manu Justo (78'). Incidencias: Partido correspondiente a la décima jornada ,disputado en Can Misses ante 1.518 espectadores. Un partido encarrilado desde el principio El Ibiza no esperó para marcar territorio. En el minuto 9, Josep Calavera abrió el marcador para establecer el 1-0 que condicionaría todo lo que vino después. El centrocampista, uno de los más destacados del encuentro con una nota de 8,3, firmó un partido completo tanto con balón como en las tareas de recuperación. Con la ventaja mínima al descanso, el Ibiza salió decidido a sentenciar tras la reanudación. En el minuto 51, Georges Nsukula culminó una jugada asistida por Theo Valls para firmar el 2-0. El tanto desató la tranquilidad en Can Misses y permitió al técnico local repartir minutos desde el banquillo. La guinda la puso Manu Justo en el minuto 78. El delantero, que había entrado al terreno de juego en el minuto 66, resolvió con precisión un balón servido por David Astals para establecer el definitivo 3-0. El gol fue revisado por el VAR y finalmente concedido en el minuto 79, confirmando la máxima goleada de la noche. El reparto de superioridad en los datos El marcador no engaña, y las estadísticas lo sostienen. El Ibiza acabó con un 56% de posesión y, sobre todo, con una diferencia abrumadora en ocasiones claras: 5 grandes ocasiones frente a la única del Europa. El dato de goles esperados —2,41 para los locales por 0,82 para los visitantes— subraya hasta qué punto el triunfo fue merecido. En el apartado de remates, el Ibiza disparó 17 veces, con 10 tiros entre los tres palos. El Europa no se escondió y llegó a los 14 disparos totales, pero solo 6 fueron a puerta y su producción ofensiva careció de la contundencia necesaria para incomodar un resultado que se le escapó pronto. La figura defensiva de la noche fue el portero local Andrés Prieto, que firmó la mejor valoración del partido con un 8,5 gracias a sus 7 paradas, 6 de ellas a disparos desde dentro del área. Su rendimiento se tradujo en 0,88 goles evitados, un número que explica por qué el Europa, pese a generar algo de volumen, se marchó sin premio. Nombres propios del Ibiza Más allá de los goleadores, el partido dejó actuaciones de nota alta en las filas celestes. El lateral Víctor García se mostró muy participativo, con 4 pases clave y 2 grandes ocasiones creadas camino de un 8,1 de valoración, mientras que Josep Calavera combinó su gol con un trabajo incansable en el centro del campo. El francés Jérémy Blasco (7,5) y Erik Ruiz (7,5) sostuvieron la línea defensiva, y la entrada de Manu Justo cambió el guion del tramo final: con apenas 24 minutos en el césped bastó para que el delantero firmara el tanto que cerró la cuenta y se marchara con un 7,4. El Europa, condenado por su falta de puntería El cuadro visitante tuvo detalles de rebeldía. Youssef Zayzoun fue su jugador más incisivo con 5 remates y una valoración de 7,8 antes de ser sustituido, y Joan Mascaró —el futbolista más seguido del once escapulado— aportó 4 regates completados y una gran ocasión creada para un 7,2. En la portería, Nil Ruiz evitó una goleada mayor con 7 paradas. Pero el Europa pagó caro su desacierto. El delantero Khalid Noureddine firmó 4 disparos sin recompensa y hasta 5 fueras de juego, mientras el equipo en conjunto desperdició la escasa claridad que generó. La diferencia entre crear y concretar separó a los dos equipos. Lo que dice la clasificación Con este triunfo, el Ibiza alcanza los 17 puntos y se asienta en la tercera posición del Grupo 2, fruto de un balance de 5 victorias, 2 empates y 3 derrotas en 10 partidos disputados. Los celestes quedan a tres puntos de los dos líderes, Villarreal B y Real Zaragoza, ambos con 20 puntos, y mantienen vivo el pulso por los puestos de privilegio. La situación del CE Europa, en cambio, se agrava. Los catalanes son decimoctavos con solo 7 puntos (2 victorias, 1 empate, 7 derrotas) tras diez jornadas, instalados de lleno en la zona de descenso y con un balance goleador muy preocupante: 6 tantos a favor por 18 en contra. La visita a Can Misses no hizo sino profundizar en una dinámica que exige una reacción inmediata. Conclusión El 3-0 fue el reflejo justo de un partido en el que el Ibiza fue superior en casi todas las facetas: más pegada, más ocasiones y una portería blindada por Andrés Prieto. Los de casa recuperan sensaciones y se mantienen en la pelea por el ascenso directo, mientras el Europa afronta las próximas jornadas con la urgencia de quien necesita puntos para salir del fondo de la tabla.

articles.title: Pau Navarro señala a la grada de La Cerámica: "No puede ser que en el minuto 75 el campo esté vacío"
articles.standfirst: El defensa amarillo pide unidad entre equipo y afición tras la derrota ante el Espanyol y pide apoyo a los hinchas hasta el final
articles.summary: El defensa amarillo pide unidad entre equipo y afición tras la derrota ante el Espanyol y pide apoyo a los hinchas hasta el final
articles.body: Tras la derrota frente al Espanyol en La Cerámica, Pau Navarro hizo autocrítica por la situación del Villarreal como local y reclamó una mayor unión entre equipo y afición para recuperar la fortaleza del estadio amarillo. El defensa lamentó la fuga de puntos en casa, insistió en la necesidad de que el equipo sea más exigente consigo mismo y considera clave el apoyo de la grada durante los momentos decisivos de los partidos. En declaraciones a Movistar, el canterano también apeló a convertir nuevamente La Cerámica en un fortín y aseguró que el grupo afronta desde ya el próximo partido de Champions ante el PSG el martes 3 de noviembre en el estadio del submarino. ¿Qué ha pasado para que el equipo vuelva a dejar escapar puntos en casa? "Hacemos cosas bien, pero la realidad es que no nos da. Tenemos que hacernos mucho más fuertes en casa. Aquí todos los años hemos sacado la mayoría de los puntos y debemos exigirnos sumar de tres cada vez aquí. Necesitamos estar muy juntos, el apoyo de la afición. No puede ser que en el minuto 75 el campo esté vacío. Tenemos que ir todos a una, eso marca la diferencia. Cuando vas a otros campos, los últimos minutos aprietan muchísimo y aquí tenemos que hacernos fuertes, tenemos que unirnos todos y debemos empezar por exigirnos nosotros dentro del campo, los que más". ¿Qué le falta al equipo para ganar en casa, teniendo una plantilla de tanta entidad? "Nos sentimos cómodos en algunas situaciones de partido y, cuando se nos encierran un poco, puede que nos falte saber jugar contra los equipos que se nos encierran un poco más. Creo que tenemos que trabajar ahí, tenemos que mover más rápido la pelota. Tenemos muy buenos jugadores arriba y tienen que marcar la diferencia. También tenemos que empezar a no encajar atrás". ¿Qué mensaje quiere transmitir a la afición del Villarreal y qué importancia tiene su apoyo? "Yo hace tres años estaba ahí arriba y sé que, cuando todos quieren, podemos hacer de este campo un fortín. Se ha demostrado, yo he estado ahí arriba y lo he visto y lo he vivido aquí abajo. Entonces, creo que debe ser la tónica de siempre en casa porque eso nos va a hacer más fuertes en la Liga, sumar aquí los máximos puntos posibles". ¿Cómo afrontan el próximo partido de Champions contra el PSG? "Vamos a salir al 100 %. Sabemos y creemos que podemos ganar esos partidos y nos vamos muy jodidos por hoy, pero tenemos partido cada tres días, pensando ya en la Champions, y esto lo sacamos". Preguntado Iñigo Pérez, técnico del Villarreal, por estas declaraciones tras el partido, fue tajante también en Movistar: "No voy a ser yo el que diga una sola palabra de la afición del Villarreal. Tenemos que mirarnos a nosotros mismos, intentar corregir aquello que nos penaliza. Los jugadores lo intentan, no tengo ningún tipo de queja, habrá que perseguirlo con más inteligencia y con más calidad".

images.caption: Pau Navarro, tras el partido ante el Espanyol. MOVISTAR

articles.title: Duncan Ferguson: From WiFi to 'relief' - How was Glentoran manager's Irish League debut?
articles.summary: After a 1-1 draw in his first match as Glentoran manager, Duncan Ferguson speaks of his "relief" in a week filled with WiFi and homework.
articles.body:
"Football is football. I've managed in the Premier League, I've managed in Scotland and I've managed here.

"The ball is still round, the goals are still in the same spot and it's still 11 v 11."

Duncan Ferguson applauded as he walked to the travelling Glentoran support after a battling 1-1 draw with Coleraine, before he gently pumped his fist into the air.

It wasn't the three points that he would have dreamt of to start his managerial career in the Irish Premiership, but a fighting point at the leaders gave an insight into what was to come.

The appointment of the former Everton striker was the most high-profile in the Irish League in recent years.

After disappointing spells with Forest Green Rovers and Inverness Caledonian Thistle, Ferguson is a manager with a point to prove at a club who also have a similar chip on their shoulder as they look to return to the heights of years gone by.

Ferguson's Glentoran reign starts with draw at Coleraine

Ferguson sees Glentoran draw in first game as manager - as it happened

After his first scheduled match as manager against Ballymena United was postponed last week due to a waterlogged pitch at the Oval, all eyes turned to Northern Ireland's north coast as 'Big Dunc' made his Irish League arrival.

The build-up to the game had been dominated by a viral video as he raced around the Oval trying to find the WiFi password in an entertaining and expletive-led fashion.

Thankfully for Ferguson, who admitted he was nervous before the game, his approach on the pitch was a lot more solid.

While Joel Cooper's superb goal broke Glentoran's resistance in a largely defensive first-half display, the visitors improved after the restart and got a deserved equaliser through Jordan Stewart's header with two minutes remaining.

"It's a relief. At the end of the day you are under pressure," said Ferguson, who also had two interim spells as Everton manager in 2019 and 2022.

"My first game didn't happen with Ballymena, and all of a sudden my next game is away at the league leaders.

"It's not easy. The boys performed great and they done their club proud."

On the touchline, bar one telling off from the fourth official, Ferguson was a largely restrained figure as he marauded around his technical area, occasionally bellowing orders to his players or giving them hearty claps of encouragement.

Coming up against a Coleraine side who were the highest scorers in the division this season, defeat would have left Glentoran some 17 points off the Bannsiders before the end of October.

With that in mind, the Scottish manager opted for a solid foundation to contain Coleraine, although he felt his side were "too passive in our shape" as Cooper, one of the league's top players, curled home a delightful opener.

Matthew Shevlin stuck the post and Glentoran goalkeeper Andrew Mills made a couple of strong saves, but the visitors pressed forwards as they started to "gamble".

As in his playing days, grit and determination were at the fore and the Glens deserved their equaliser as Stewart's late header rescued a point.

For one of the smallest players on the pitch, who Ferguson has already named "the wee man", it was a finish the former Everton and Newcastle United striker would have been proud of.

"They have a lot of attacking threats but, aside from the boy sticking one in the top corner, we restricted them in the first half.

"We've come to the best team in the league and in the second half I felt we went toe-to-toe with them."

Ferguson added that he had a "good gauge" of Ruaidhri Higgins' side before the game, and the response shown by his side bodes well going forward.

"It took a lot of determination and resilience to get back into the match and I'm pleased with that.

"I knew they were a good team. If you had offered me a draw before the match I would have taken it, 100%."

Ferguson has been open about his lack of knowledge of the Irish Premiership before his appointment, and has been leaning on the likes of Elliott Morris and Andy Matheson at the Oval to build his expertise.

But he has bought into his new role so far. On Saturday, after his first match was postponed, he went to Seaview to watch Coleraine's win over Crusaders, and he was also at a Glentoran Under-20s match at Dungannaon Swifts during the week.

After passing his first test at the league leaders, Ferguson admits he will "be back on his homework" on Saturday before his second game, away to Carrick Rangers.

"It's all one game at a time, but we've got a bit of time to prepare for Carrick Rangers.

"It's not all about tactics, it's about fire, determination and about running. My players showed that in the second half."

articles.title: Levante vs Atlético: Maldición antes de la tormenta
articles.standfirst: Hoy, la antesala de sus choques en el Metropolitano ante Bayern y Barça • Los valencianos, a dos puntos de todo
articles.summary: Hoy, la antesala de sus choques en el Metropolitano ante Bayern y Barça • Los valencianos, a dos puntos de todo
articles.body: Tres empates, seis puntos que vuelan. Ese es el balance de las tres últimas visitas del Atlético en un Ciutat en el que esta tarde, a la hora de la comida, intentará la que sería su séptima victoria seguida en LaLiga. Un triunfo necesario que, además, le permitiría ser líder… al menos hasta que el Barça juegue su partido ante el Levante apenas cinco horas después de que acabe el choque en la capital del Turia. Los del Cholo están firmando el tercer mejor arranque de su historia gracias a que este curso son fiables a domicilio. Salvo el traspiés de San Mamés, cuentan por victoria todos sus partidos. Triunfos en campos complicados como Anoeta y el Pizjuán por más de un gol de ventaja. Triunfos también sobre la bocina en las casas de Alavés y Espanyol gracias a goles finales de Cuti Romero y Baena, que rescataron dos victorias que permiten a los rojiblancos mirar por encima del Real Madrid tras la jornada 10. El central argentino y el ex del Villarreal serán dos de los titulares de un Atlético que dará vuelo a casi todos sus titulares. Los Llorente, Giuliano, Julián y cía no descansarán pese a lo que viene después, ni más ni menos que Bayern y Barcelona en dos choques que pueden aclarar la clasificación en Champions (acercando o alejando el top 8, objetivo final antes de los cruces) y en LaLiga (de ganar al Levante saldría líder de ese partido si doblega a los de Flick dentro de una semana en el Metropolitano). Todo ello, claro, después de enfrentarse a la maldición del Ciutat. El Levante buscará esta tarde la tercera victoria de la temporada, tras caer derrotado ante la Real Sociedad el pasado fin de semana. A pesar del rojo, los valencianos se encuentran en una zona tranquila, a dos puntos del descenso y a otros tantos de las posiciones que dieron acceso, el año pasado, a posiciones europeas. Para este envite, Luís Castro recupera a un efectivo muy importante en la parte defensiva, como es Dela, aunque mantendrá una semana más apartado por lesión al francés Enzo Badeli en el centro del campo. En un partido con malos recuerdos para el técnico argentino del Atlético de Madrid, los valencianos intentarán meter presión y sumar puntos en su casillero, como ya ha ocurrido en las últimas tres visitas de los capitalinos al Ciutat, en el que se saldó con tres empates consecutivos que convierten este estadio en uno de los que peor se les da a los delCholo.De ahí lo de maldición.

articles.title: Wrexham news: Red Dragons need honest self-assessment - Parkinson
articles.summary: Phil Parkinson says he will not shy away from any criticism that comes his way following Wrexham's 1-0 Championship loss to Sheffield United at Bramall Lane.
articles.body:
Phil Parkinson says Wrexham need to conduct some "honest" self-assessments on the back of their lacklustre display against Sheffield United.

The Red Dragons were significantly below par at Bramall Lane, particularly in the first half, as Ben Brereton Diaz's 30th-minute strike earned the Blades a 1-0 victory.

After the defeat in South Yorkshire, Parkinson urged his players to be individually "self-analytical".

"However you play, it's about 11 v 11, winning your individual duels and coming out on top of the player you're against," he told BBC Radio Wales.

"I'll always look at myself and my contributions, I'm the manager and obviously it's a significant one.

"But equally, I said to the lads, the first 45 minutes, we made them look a really good side.

"We've got to be very honest and self-analytical individually about our own performances and make sure that when we turn up on Wednesday night (against Middlesbrough) that we are ready to go toe-to-toe with a top team."

Sheffield United earn narrow win over Wrexham in Championship

Wrexham fined for fielding ineligible players

Wrexham did not manage a single shot on target until Sam Smith's tame header was easily saved by Michael Cooper in the 96th minute.

They made just nine passes in the final third in the opening half, 68 fewer than Chris Wilder's men managed in the same period.

"We were second best in the first 45 minutes," added Parkinson.

"I just said to the lads in there that we played Sheffield United as a National League team at home (in 2023), we went to war with them, toe-to-toe, 3-3.

"We came here in midweek, everyone thought they'd have too much for us, we put in an unbelievable performance with a lot lesser team than we had tonight.

"Our performances this season, there have been some good ones.

"But we haven't got that Wrexham feel into every performance, which is that everybody wants to beat us, and an underdog mentality, a siege mentality."

Parkinson has overseen immense success since being named as Wrexham boss in the summer of 2021.

He guided the club to three successive promotions between 2023 and 2025, although the pressure appears to be mounting on the 58-year-old following a slow start to the current campaign.

The Red Dragons have lost three of their past four matches and face promotion-hopefuls Middlesbrough and Wolverhampton Wanderers in their final two matches prior to the November international window.

On the back of Wrexham's poor showing in Sheffield, Parkinson stated he would not hide away from any criticism that comes his way over the coming days.

"I'll just deal with it (criticism) like I've always dealt with it, I'll just concentrate on what I've got to do," he said.

"What can I do? Curl up in a ball and not come out of the house for three days?

"I've built my career as a manager and a player on fighting and being resilient.

"I've been dropped as a player, I've been sacked as a manager, I've lost games as a manager, I've had supporters chanting for me to be sacked.

"I've got thick skin, but equally, if I was a supporter, I'd be very disappointed in the way the lads played in that first 45 minutes.

"So if there is criticism, then we certainly can't hide away from that, and I won't."

articles.body: El Barcelona vuelve hoy al Spotify Camp Nou. Lo hace tras la derrota en el Clásico de la anterior jornada. El Barça se ha rearmado moralmente durante la semana. Hansi Flick ha trabajado con sus hombres el plano anímico y estos incluso han realizado una comida de hermandad envuelta de conjura para dejar atrás la derrota contra el PSG y sobre todo la del Clásico. Se creen fuertes para volver a la senda de los triunfos y para seguir liderando la tabla. Pero para el cruce contra el Alavés, Flick está obligado a modificar su línea defensiva. El Barcelona afronta el compromiso con seis bajas, cuatro de ellas en la zaga. El conjunto catalán no puede disponer de Christensen, Eric García, Koundé y Xavi Espart. Ante estas ausencias, el técnico, que ha citado a jóvenes del fútbol base para completar la convocatoria, apostará, a priori, contra los de Quique Sánchez Flores por Brian, en la derecha; Cubarsí y Gerard Martín en el eje, y Cancelo en la izquierda. articles.title: Jamie Carragher sued: Aston Villa to take legal action against pundit over 'unacceptable insults'
articles.summary: Aston Villa say they will initiate legal action against Jamie Carragher over what the club branded as "unacceptable insults".
articles.body:
Aston Villa say they will initiate legal action against Jamie Carragher over what the club branded as "unacceptable insults".

Posting on their social media on Friday, Villa released a statement signed by their chairman Nassef Sawiris accusing Carragher of insulting the Premier League side and its fans.

It added the club would "not allow anyone to stop our ascension in English and European football".

Speaking on the Stick to Football podcast, Carragher attracted criticism from Villa fans by suggesting their manager Unai Emery would be interested in becoming Manchester United 's head coach.

Michael Carrick's position at United is hanging in the balance after a dismal start to the campaign and Carragher said " Aston Villa will never be Manchester United ".

"Surely he would want that opportunity to manage a giant again," Carragher said.

"There is a chain in football, whether you like it or not.

"So Real Madrid will take Manchester United 's best player, they did it with [Cristiano] Ronaldo.

"And there will be teams below Aston Villa , and they'll take their players or manager, so shut the [expletive] up Aston Villa fans. Aston Villa will never be Manchester United ."

Carragher, a football pundit for works for Sky Sports and American broadcaster CBS, has already commented on the backlash he received after he told the fans to shut up.

"It was a joke after the stick Villa fans have given me over saying Emery may fancy joining Man Utd," Carragher said on social media.

"I hope these clown clips show me praising Emery/Villa like I have done for years & saying how pleased I was you won [the 2026 Europa League] in Istanbul."

On the Overlap Daily, Carragher went into more detail.

"I just think Unai Emery is the best manager in the league and if you're Man Utd you're thinking 'what's the best we can get?'. I'm not saying he'll go - I'm just saying if it was me I'd ask the question," said Carragher.

"Certain managers are good at certain clubs and that's Emery. He reminds me of Rafa [Benitez]. I think your own ego if someone said 'that's your level' would say 'no I'm not'. That was my point.

"It's grew arms and legs. I ended up telling them to [expletive] which maybe I shouldn't have done but it was all in jest because they've been all over my social timeline. I was saying [expletive] off my socials."

articles.title: Bill Belichick and Jordon Hudson reportedly broke up in late 2025, but still 'committed to their business partnerships'
articles.summary: One of the most-scrutinized romances in sports is reportedly over.
articles.body:
UNC head coach Bill Belichick and his girlfriend Jordon Hudson broke up in late 2025, according to a report from TMZ .

The specifics of the breakup are unclear, including who initiated it, but it was apparently amicable enough that TMZ says they are told the pair remain "committed to their business partnerships and remain close friends."

There has been no public indication the much-publicized relationship has ended, as Hudson has remained on the UNC sidelines at games this year. Her most recent Instagram post, dated May 2, features the two holding hands at the Kentucky Derby, with the caption "Not the first time we've trudged through the mud together."

Belichick, 73, and Hudson first met on a flight in 2021 and went public with their relationship in 2024 while the six-time Super Bowl winner spent the season out of coaching.

By May 2025, The New York Times was reporting that Hudson had told at least one person that she and Belichick were engaged. The relationship reportedly ended months later, though Hudson has continued to work alongside Belichick essentially as his brand manager.

Jordon Hudson was a central figure in Bill Belichick's life, and apparently still is

The initial reactions to Belichick and Hudson's relationship in 2024 ranged from shock to amusement over the nearly five-decade age gap — Hudson was born in 2001, months before Belichick's first Super Bowl-winning season with the New England Patriots.

Hudson's role in Belichick's professional life first received scrutiny in April 2025 when she curtly interrupted a Belichick interview with "CBS Sunday Morning" after the coach was asked about how the two met. Belichick defended Hudson in the aftermath of the interview, and said that she was "simply doing her job to ensure the interview stayed on track."

Belichick was doing the interview to promote his book, however CBS said that no topic was off-limits as part of the discussion.

Not long after the CBS interview was released, North Carolina denied a report from the "Pablo Torre Finds Out" podcast that Hudson had been banned from the North Carolina football facilities. In its statement, UNC said that Hudson was "welcome to the Carolina Football facilities" and that she would "continue to manage all activities related to Coach Belichick's personal brand."

Hudson has been widely reported to have never had an official role at UNC, working instead as a manager for Belichick's own business operations.

That management extended to the now-shelved docu-series that was going to follow North Carolina during its tumultuous 2025 season. The Hulu series was scrapped after North Carolina failed to beat a power conference opponent over the first half of the season. The contracts for the series detailed that Belichick could stop production at any time by retracting his consent to cooperate and Hudson signed one of them as the COO of TCE Rights Management LLC regarding Belichick's own image rights.

Hudson hasn't received quite as much publicity in 2026, which has been a more successful season for UNC through seven games. The school's record is 4-3, which includes Belichick's first ranked win over No. 25 Pitt .

The Tar Heels play No. 1 Miami on Saturday.

articles.title: Iñigo: “Debo encontrar soluciones porque no estamos siendo convincentes”
articles.standfirst: El técnico del Villarreal no busca excusas a la mala dinámica como locales
articles.summary: El técnico del Villarreal no busca excusas a la mala dinámica como locales
articles.body: Iñigo no eludió la autocrítica a la hora de referirse a una actuación poco convincente” y a la necesidad urgente de dar un cambio de rumbo radical a la situación de su equipo en La Cerámica. El navarro aseguró que le preocupa que su equipo se frustre cuando juega como local Frenazo: “Hoy es un es un frenazo, es un momento difícil porque hay que asimilarlo y después del partido es difícil. No hemos hablado nada sinceramente, pero no hace falta hablar mucho. El silencio habla solo y estamos un poco decepcionados con lo que hemos podido ofrecer” Menos finos: “Dominamos, controlamos el esférico, generamos más ocasiones, a lo mejor hoy no tan claras como en el partido ante el Elche. Pero a la hora de la verdad, ellos llegan dos veces, nos meten un gol y nosotros la sensación que, al menos se transmitía desde el campo, es que podíamos remar, remar, remar, pero daba la sensación de que no que no avanzábamos. Creo que no hemos estado tan finos como otras veces en las que las llegadas obtenidas eran muy claras, creo que hemos dispuesto de ellas como para no perder el partido, pero no es una excusa, no caeré en ese error. Debemos encontrar, debo encontrar las soluciones, puesto que no están siendo actuaciones ni convincentes, ni contundentes para generar victorias” No caer en la precipitación: “Creo que hay que diferenciar dos posturas, una es la de ir a la tremenda, que los días que hemos intentado hacer eso, hemos salido escaldados. Como ante el Betis o el día del Depor , y otra es intentar tomar ciertos riesgos, controlados que lo hemos hecho en otros partidos y aún así tampoco quizá hemos obtenido lo que merecías. La búsqueda de las soluciones es la clave, tengo que insistir, tendremos que cambiar cosas, tendremos que permanecer en esa lucha interna y esperar que esto cambie. Esa desesperación, esa pérdida posicional, ese salir del plan, creo que el entrenador, a pesar de tener ahora todo ardiendo, debe mantener la cabeza fría y tampoco podemos alterar los planes, pero sí, la búsqueda de soluciones para poder poder cambiar la dinámica. Le preocupa que caigan en la frustración: “Sí, me preocupa. Me preocupa primero por ellos, porque sé cómo son, ya les voy conociendo y entiendo perfectamente el momento en el que entran en esa fase. un poco de niebla. Pero muchas veces por pegar muy fuerte o por insistir mucho de una manera que no es la adecuada no llega. Tampoco ha llegado cuando lo hemos hecho bien. Entonces, ahí está el dilema. Pero sí, me preocupa, no quiero que pierdan el eje, no quiero que se salgan de lo que ellos hacen bien porque si no es más difícil. Baja puntuación: “La puntuación está claro que no es la deseada, no es la que buscamos y no es la que nos da los objetivos a final de temporada y por eso venimos hablando de esa rueda de prensa de intentar revertirla. Sobre la falta de un organizador: “Pienso que los datos ofensivos del equipo desde el inicio hasta ahora en cuanto a generación de juego, posesión, etcétera, hacen ver que todos los jugadores que juegan en medio campo son capaces de generar flujo ofensivo. Por tanto, no creo que estemos necesitados de otro perfil, creo que los mediocentros del equipo tienen mucho nivel. Y aparte, generar juego ofensivo, no depende únicamente de ellos. No creo que sea la solución ahora mismo. Desacierto de los atacantes: “Hay dos vertientes. Una que los equipos rivales, fruto del dominio que tenemos, se encierran en el área y es más difícil encontrar los espacios o las soluciones. Hay más ayudas, hay más piernas, hay más cuerpos y es más difícil. Pero también hay una parte mental, de ver que no estás todo lo fino que quieres y que no están haciendo los goles que en algún momento han hecho en esas mismas circunstancias. Tengo la sensación de que vamos a seguir generando ocasiones y encerrando al rival y la segunda es un poco cómo encontrar el partido, encontrar los momentos en los que entren dinámicas buenas para ellos, que hagan goles y que cojan esa línea de actuación” Lesión de Gerard: “Ahora es precipitado adelantar cuál es el diagnóstico, el certero, pero cuando Gerard me pide el cambio de manera tan temprana, seguro que algo ha notado. Ojalá que no que no sea mucho y que su experiencia en este tipo de vicisitudes, pues le hagan haber tomado un poco de resguardo y que podamos contar con él pronto”
